title: Rating Office Basis for a Re-Rating on a Travel Protection Certificate
content:
Where a declared particular of the risk on a certificate of the Travel Protection Plans has changed after
issue, the premium is re-rated, and the difference between the premium the certificate now rates to and the
premium the record shows collected is charged over the days of cover still to run.

## The quantities

| Quantity | What it is |
|---|---|
| The rate applied | The plan's base rate as a proportion of the declared trip cost, increased by the plan's destination loading percentage of that base rate |
| The premium the certificate now rates to | The declared trip cost standing on the certificate multiplied by the rate applied, rounded to two decimal places at that step |
| The premium the record shows collected | The figure the policy record shows paid |
| The difference | The premium the certificate now rates to less the premium the record shows collected, never less than nothing |
| The day the change takes effect | The day the certificate was issued |
| The days of cover still to run | Counted from the day the change takes effect to the last date of the journey, both counted, and never less than nothing |
| The days of cover bought | The days of the journey, its first and last both counted |

The difference is then taken in the proportion the days of cover still to run bear to the days of cover bought,
and never charged in full where cover has already begun to run. The charge is never less than nothing and is
rounded to two decimal places once, at the end, no intermediate figure being rounded.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A plan whose base rate is 6.8 per cent and whose destination loading percentage is 20 gives a rate applied of
8.16 per cent of the declared trip cost. On a certificate now declaring a trip cost of 9000.00, the premium the
certificate now rates to is 734.40, rounded at that step. The policy record shows 612.00 paid, so the difference
is 122.40.

The certificate was issued on the 1st, the journey runs from the 10th to the 19th, and the change takes effect
on the day the certificate was issued. The days of cover bought are 10, the 10th and the 19th both counted. The
days of cover still to run are counted from the 1st to the 19th, both counted, and come to 19. The difference
taken in the proportion 19 bears to 10 gives 232.56, and the charge is 232.56. The figures and dates are
hypothetical.
